name: Kizilay
tagline: The city's central square, students and cheap eating
description: Ankara's functional heart, where the metro lines cross and where the bookshops, cheap restaurants, student bars and political life of the capital concentrate. It is dense, loud and entirely practical, with the ministries a short walk south and everything reachable on the metro.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the metro, the bookshops and cheap eating on the doorstep
pros: Both metro lines and every bus route
Dense cheap restaurants and student bars
Everything practical within a short walk
cons: Loud, crowded and short of green space
Demonstrations and heavy policing at times

name: Cankaya and Kavaklidere
tagline: The embassy districts, leafier and considerably calmer
description: The southern hillside where the embassies, the better restaurants and the wine bars of Tunali Hilmi sit among tree-lined streets. It is the most comfortable part of Ankara, with the largest concentration of foreign residents and the best food in the city.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a calm district and the international community
pros: The best restaurants and wine bars in the city
Embassies and the international community nearby
cons: Heavy security presence around some embassies

name: Ulus and the Citadel
tagline: The old town below the walls, with the best museum in Turkey
description: The historic core around the Ottoman citadel, holding the Museum of Anatolian Civilisations, the Roman temple, the old bazaar and the surviving timber houses inside the walls. It is the oldest and cheapest part of Ankara and by a distance the most interesting to walk.
bestFor: Budget stays that want the citadel and the museums rather than the modern city
pros: The Museum of Anatolian Civilisations on the doorstep
Genuine Ottoman streets inside the walls
cons: Run down in parts and less comfortable at night

name: Bahcelievler and Emek
tagline: The university belt around Hacettepe and the campuses
description: The western residential districts around the universities, with the seventh street bar strip, cheap student restaurants and low-rise apartment buildings. It has the liveliest and cheapest social life in Ankara and a population that is overwhelmingly under twenty-five.
bestFor: Budget stays that want the student bars and the cheapest central rents
pros: Cheap student bars and restaurants throughout
Metro and buses into the centre

name: Cayyolu and the Western Suburbs
tagline: New apartment complexes out west, space and quiet
description: The planned residential expansion west of the city along the metro extension, with modern gated apartment complexes, supermarkets, schools and considerably more space than anything central. It is where Ankara's professional families have moved, and the metro takes about half an hour into Kizilay.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting a modern, well-built flat and quiet
pros: Metro line direct into the centre
Cleaner air and more green space
cons: Half an hour to the centre
Car-dependent for anything off the metro
Generic and short on street life
